split_identity.note: 5 people are on two sites' rosters as separate employees, and neither site knows. On the days they are at one site, the other logs a no-show and pays someone to cover it — 39 times in 10 weeks, 14 of them provably while the person was clocked in at their other site. The same double booking also put ~510 hours on the books at two sites at once — hours that cannot be trusted for payroll. Fix: make each a single-site employee, drop them from the other site, and spread that post across the under-used same-role staff already there.

under_recording.note: 184 shifts (2.1%) were clocked in but never clocked out and are logged as 0h — most carry cover notes. Shift length caps at 13.5h (366 shifts sit exactly there), so a genuine 20-hour double is recorded as 13.5h or 0h. A no-show creates no record at all. Net: a no-show removes recorded hours for that site-day even though the same coverage was delivered — so operational-failure overtime, and the breach risk of the people who cover, is understated. Recorded breach rate 5.0%; imputing one shift per open-shift week puts it at ~5.6%.
